subject: Availability SLA addendum request + order form language (LabSync)
messages:
From: Alyssa Turner <alyssa.turner@labsync.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: LabSync Legal <legal@labsync.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 15:20:00 -0800
Subject: SLA addendum: availability & latency commitments for enterprise SOW

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the demo last week — LabSync is excited about Redwood for embedding and model serving. Our procurement team is preparing the contract packet (MSA + SOW + order form) and we've hit one snag: we need a custom SLA addendum that covers availability and latency commitments for our production workloads. High level asks: 

- Availability: target 99.95% monthly uptime for the production API endpoints used by LabSync (customer-facing).
- Latency: p99 <= 150ms for typical single-turn generation at ~1k tokens; we'd accept higher for long-run or streaming calls but want clear bounds.
- Exception windows: we need defined maintenance windows and a process for emergency maintenance; also a mechanism for requesting a temporary exception for scheduled infrastructure migrations.

We're aiming to include the addendum as an attachment to the SOW (see attached LabSync_MSA_Draft_v3.pdf). Can you:

1) Confirm whether Redwood can commit to these targets under a Dedicated or Private deployment?
2) Provide suggested order-form language we can include that ties credits/penalties to uptime targets and latency SLO misses.
3) Confirm escalation contacts and RTO/RPO expectations for incidents that affect availability.

If possible, please send a draft addendum and the order-form snippet by end of week so our legal can fold it into the packet. We're aiming to finalize commercial terms the week of Dec 7.

Thanks — copying our legal email for visibility.

Best,
Alyssa Turner
Head of Platform Engineering | LabSync
alyssa.turner@labsync.ai
Attachment: LabSync_MSA_Draft_v3.pdf (PDF, 1 page - MSA highlights)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Turner <alyssa.turner@labsync.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLA addendum: availability & latency commitments for enterprise SOW

Alyssa — thanks for the clear ask and for sharing the draft MSA. Short answers up front: yes, we can support custom uptime & latency commitments, but the commitments and remedies differ across Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Dedicated (reserved GPU capacity) or Private (VPC/on-prem) are the paths where we can most confidently offer 99.95% uptime and tighter latency SLOs with measurable credits.

Next steps / what I attached: 
- rishi_labsync_sla_addendum_draft.docx — a working draft addendum that includes availability targets, credit table, and a proposed maintenance/exception clause.
- orderform_snippet.txt — short text you can drop into the order form that enumerates the SLA, deployment type (Dedicated), and committed throughput class.

A few quick clarifications we need from you to finalize the language: 
- Expected qps and burst characteristics (avg and 95th percentile).
- Typical request size (tokens) and how often you use long-context streaming. That affects our kernel selection & latency guarantees.
- Whether you require multi-region active/active (reduces single-region downtime exposure).

Operational notes: 
- Our standard maintenance window is Sundays 02:00–06:00 UTC; we can negotiate a fixed window or allow scheduled exceptions documented in the SOW. Emergency maintenance is rare; where it happens we commit to advance notice when feasible and an incident timeline with RCA.
- Credits: the draft uses a proportional credit model (days under target => credit % of monthly fee). Happy to adjust to a per-incident cap.

Copying Lauren (legal) and Marissa (CS/solutions) for contractual and technical redlines. If you like, we can schedule a 30-min call this week to walk the teams through the proposed addendum.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Sales, Enterprise | Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0126
Attachments: rishi_labsync_sla_addendum_draft.docx (Word, 2 pages), orderform_snippet.txt (TXT, 1 page)

Alyssa / Rishi — looping in a couple of quick legal points and redlines so you have visibility before LabSync folds language into the MSA: 

1) Remedy structure: our standard is service credits as the exclusive remedy for SLA breaches. Legal would prefer a capped credit (e.g., not to exceed 100% of one month’s fees) and to avoid unlimited liability.
2) Latency SLOs: we want to limit latency SLOs to specific API routes and model families (e.g., generation-v1 class). For longer stream sessions or >8k token decoding, we need explicit carve-outs.
3) Maintenance/Exception: propose this clause: "Planned maintenance shall not exceed X windows per quarter and shall be notified 72 hours in advance; emergency maintenance shall be communicated as soon as practicable and is not considered a breach if impact is limited to <Y minutes per incident and documented in the incident report."

Marissa — could you confirm operational feasibility of the 99.95% target on Dedicated for the workloads Rishi referenced? If LabSync plans to push >200 qps / sustained bursts we should recommend Dedicated capacity with autoscale.

Alyssa — once we have expected traffic profile (qps/tokens), we can produce a final addendum that includes both the credit table and the SLO definitions.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Legal | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Attachment: legal_redlines_labsync.pdf (PDF, 3 pages - redline comments)

Rishi / Lauren / team — thank you for the quick turnaround and the draft addendum. LabSync reviewed the proposed language and legal redlines. We have two small follow-ups: 

- Credits: we can accept a capped credit but would like the cap at 100% of the monthly fee if monthly uptime drops below 99.0% (we're asking for this to be an exception tier).
- Escalations: please confirm the named escalation contacts and that we can get a 24x7 escalation channel for severity 1 incidents (pager or phone).

If you can confirm both of those items and incorporate Lauren's redline for maintenance notification, we can accept the addendum and move the SOW to signature via DocuSign. We'll route the final packet to legal this afternoon and expect to complete signatures mid-next week.

Appreciate everyone's help — we can take the 30-min walkthrough if helpful but I think the doc is near-final.

Best,
